ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of each UBO, director, officer and 5%-or-greater shareholder against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada), the Special Economic Measures Act schedules, the Criminal Code s. 83.05 listed terrorist entities, the United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, and the OFAC SDN list for any USD Swift wire or documentary letter-of-credit rails; PEP status must be verified using a commercial risk database with documented results retained for at least five years per FINTRAC record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) official government portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; alternative federal Corporations Canada and NUANS portal: https://www.ic.gc.ca (use only if federal CBCA articles are selected instead of provincial QBCA articles)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11: the French form of the corporate name is the official registered name; any non-French version may be used only in addition to and with equal or lesser prominence than the French version; all corporate instruments, by-laws and supply contracts must be available in French; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for registration; the legal ending must be a French or bilingual corporate designation such as Societe par actions, Inc., Corporation, Ltee, Limitee or their accepted abbreviations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: MEDICAL / SANTE (health services terms requiring ministerial approval)
PUBLICITE (advertising terms requiring Office quebecois de la langue francaise permit)
words contrary to public order, obscene or scandalous terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects or modifies the proposed name, the applicant may: (1) file a new name-reservation request online without prejudice; (2) submit a written administrative reconsideration request (demande de revision) within 30 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, s. 23, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, a prior consent letter from the existing rights holder, or a Canadian or foreign trademark registration certificate; (3) if reconsideration is refused, apply for judicial review before the Court of Quebec within 30 days of receipt of the refusal notice; for a federal CBCA name, a parallel appeal to the Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act is available within 60 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A postal-only or mail-forwarding virtual office is not accepted: the QBCA requires a physical registered office within the Province of Quebec where legal process may be served and the statutory registers, including the register of individuals with significant control, may be inspected; a managed serviced office with a physical suite, reception and professional mail-handling services is acceptable for this wholesale green coffee import trade, provided the address is not a Canada Post post-office box and the corporate minute book remains accessible at the registered office or another location in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximate 2-5% annual probability of an REQ address-verification or legal-publicity compliance visit for this low-risk containerized wholesale distribution trade; probability increases to 10-15% upon the first CRA GST/HST registration review or any FINTRAC suspicious-transaction report; no mandatory physical commodity or premises inspection applies to containerized green coffee at the pre-incorporation stage.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable discharge or emissions standards for wholesale coffee bean distribution; comply with general waste management regulations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with Quebec Occupational Health and Safety Act; no specific civil defense or fire safety certification required for coffee distribution operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST via My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-portal.html); Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) via clicSÉEQ Affaires (cliceqaffaires.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation not resident in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number from CRA and a GST/HST program account before making taxable supplies in Canada, using CRA online registration or Form RC1. If the foreign corporation carries on business in Quebec, it must separately register with Revenu Québec for a Quebec Business Number (NEQ) and a QST account; registration is completed through Revenu Québec's online business portal and requires evidence of foreign corporate existence, Canadian address for service, and contact person or representative if no place of business in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxable person; a resident corporation is subject to federal and Quebec income tax on worldwide income; non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada are subject to tax on Canadian-source income, with no general tax-exempt zone regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election for business corporations; incorporation creates a per se taxable entity. Available elections relevant to non-residents include the option under Income Tax Act section 216 to file a return for Canadian rental or timber income at a flat rate and section 217 for certain Canadian employment or scholarship income, with corresponding Quebec provisions. Hybrid mismatch adjustments apply automatically under ITA sections 18.4 to 18.6 and Quebec's Tax Administration Act, not by elective check-the-box.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT-equivalent) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable worldwide supplies in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; Revenu Québec applies the same CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction controls exist at the federal or Quebec level for general distributions. Registered persons must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST and QST details, retain electronic records, and file returns electronically; Revenu Québec imposes sales-recording and certified-bookkeeping obligations for specified businesses above turnover thresholds, but universal e-invoicing clearance is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated for GST/HST/QST if the supplier exports the goods as part of the supply and retains contemporaneous documentary proof of physical export; unroasted green coffee beans physically exported from Canada are zero-rated. Offshore services are zero-rated when rendered to a non-resident and not performed in connection with Canadian real property or goods to be consumed in Canada. The exporter must demonstrate, through shipping and banking records, that the goods left Canada and the consideration was received from outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export declaration via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) / B13A declaration, where required
Bill of Lading or air waybill, together with shipping instructions and carrier certificate of export
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the green coffee beans, quantities, marks, numbers, and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/foreign-exchange evidence of receipt of funds from the foreign buyer
Exporter's internal zero-rating support worksheet evidencing the date of export and linkage to the invoice
Export permits, certificates of origin, or phytosanitary certificates if the destination jurisdiction or controlled-goods rules require them
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated claim, deny the zero-rating benefit, and charge uncollected or ineligible GST/HST and QST together with interest from the date the return was filed. Penalties include failure-to-file and gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of the net tax understated, as well as possible criminal prosecution and cancellation of registration for fraudulent export zero-rating claims. The exporter must retain export and foreign-currency evidence for at least six years and must demonstrate that the goods were actually exported and sold to an arm's-length non-resident; absent this, the invoice may be treated as taxable and the entire tax becomes collectible.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — Canada's central monetary authority but not a foreign exchange control administrator; FX/AML reporting is administered by FINTRAC, prudential bank conduct by OSFI, and trade documentation by the Canada Border Services Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; there are no surrender requirements, exchange allocation queues, or central-bank FX approval for importers. Profit remittances by a Quebec business corporation are unrestricted at the exchange-control level, but a non-resident parent's dividend, interest, royalty, or management-fee remittance may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (statutory rates, reduced by applicable tax treaty) and must satisfy Quebec corporate solvency requirements before declaring dividends.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for exporting entities' hard-currency receipts; export proceeds may remain in any currency and no surrender obligation exists. Mandatory compliance is limited to CBSA export declarations (e.g., B13A process for controlled or specially listed goods) and FINTRAC's electronic funds transfer reporting threshold (CAD 10,000) plus financial sanctions screening under Global Affairs Canada.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account
Operational Account and FX Hedging Account
Operational Account and Commercial Letter of Credit Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for stand-alone use by a Quebec-incorporated importer. An offshore digital EMI that accepts deposits or provides money transfer services in Canada must typically register with FINTRAC as a money services business and, if operating in Quebec, obtain a Quebec money-services business registration; an unregistered offshore EMI cannot access Canadian domestic clearing rails (Payment Canada ACSS/Lynx) and will be treated by Canadian banks as a non-account counterparty. Use only as a supplemental, pre-funded remittance channel with traceable SWIFT traces and full audit trails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal law mandates that directors physically appear, but most Tier 1 Canadian banks require, as a matter of account policy, at least one verified director or authorized signatory with a Canadian identity nexus; a virtual interview and electronic identity verification may be accepted for low-risk corporate clients. For a Quebec business corporation with non-resident ownership and international green-coffee trade flows, banks often require a remote video meeting plus notarized corporate documentation; a local bank meeting can replace the video step, but physical attendance by every director is not normally demanded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-risk or sanctions-exposed source jurisdictions for green coffee purchases (e.g., payments to origin-country exporters through third-country correspondent banks).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier KYC file (registration, tax ID, physical address), fully signed coffee supply contract, commercial invoice with HS 0901.11 classification, ocean/air bill of lading, phytosanitary certificate, International Coffee Organization certificate of origin, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions screening, and a written explanation of the payment routing and economic rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, or a foreign parent controlling the Quebec corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Register of individuals with significant control, shareholder register certified by corporate counsel, certificate of incumbency attesting signatories, UBO identity and address proofs, notarized attestation of ownership chain, organizational chart, board resolution authorizing capital injection and account opening, plus source-of-funds evidence for the equity contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-value prepayments to suppliers before documentary evidence of shipment, or payments to third parties outside the coffee supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed letters of credit or separate trade-finance agreements, prepayment policy approved by the board, aged payables report, insurance on goods, supplier confirmations on letterhead, customs broker entry records, and transaction-specific commercial invoices justifying each disbursement; all supplementary payments must be mapped to named contract counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign parent injects share capital by SWIFT MT103 wire to the Quebec corporation's Canadian dollar account using the entity's corporate legal name and bank account; Canada has no central FX license requirement, but the bank's AML/KYC team may request a board resolution, source-of-funds evidence, and a payment purpose narrative stating 'capital contribution for share subscription'. The non-resident parent should confirm whether an Investment Canada Act notice or review threshold is triggered, and all inward transfers above CAD 10,000 remain reportable by the bank to FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers for supplier settlement and SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary commercial letters of credit for larger contract parcels, typically confirmed by the beneficiary bank in the coffee-origin country. Domestic ancillary disbursements (duties, freight, warehouse, customs brokerage) clear through Payment Canada ACSS/Lynx; clean-outward FX trades are subject to bank credit limits and ISDA/CSA documentation if derivatives are used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD outright forward contracts with a Schedule I Canadian bank or authorized foreign exchange dealer, evidenced by a master confirmation agreement and used only to hedge genuine commercial coffee-import exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for origin-country currencies that lack a fully convertible onshore forward market, permitted when the underlying obligation is an actual green-coffee purchase or freight/supply cost denominated in that currency.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD against USD or origin-disbursement currency) limited to financing and working-capital structures supporting import letters of credit and supplier advance payments.
Plain-vanilla FX options and call/put combinations purchased for hedging coffee purchase commitments, subject to ISDA/CSA counterparty credit documentation and confirmation of no speculative intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct late fee, but continued default prompts a notice of default from the Director and may lead to administrative dissolution under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle des societes) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end; if no fiscal year, within 60 days after the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing charges prescribed by REQ plus public notice of default; continuing failure may lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, with financial statements and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete late month, maximum 12 months; interest accrues from the balance-due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (form CO-17) and related provincial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year, aligned with the federal filing due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty and interest on unpaid provincial tax; persistent non-filing may trigger enforcement measures and corporate deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a non-distributing private business corporation in Quebec or under the CBCA, there is no mandatory annual audit solely based on revenue or asset thresholds; an auditor is appointed at each annual meeting unless the shareholders validly waive the appointment. A full statutory audit becomes compulsory only if the corporation is a reporting issuer or is otherwise regulated under securities or financial institution legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements may be prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), as adopted in the CPA Canada Handbook; tax returns must be reconciled to the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A share transfer under the Quebec Business Corporations Act is effective for corporate purposes only after entry in the Register of Members; directors must approve the transfer and promptly update the share register and minute book. The annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises is the annual confirmation event for corporate particulars, but Quebec does not require a separate annual UBO return for ordinary private corporations; accurate UBO records must be kept and disclosed to FINTRAC, CRA and Revenu Quebec on request or during AML and tax verification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Securities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approx. USD 550 - USD 1,750 per year depending on Montreal registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approx. USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a full independent audit; lower if shareholder waiver is in place or a review engagement is accepted
